answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to recurring proof of useful work. Every agent must regularly complete a verifiable computation hashed into its identity record, like a comet returning on a fixed orbit: cheap for one real agent, ruinous at scale for thousands of fakes. Each proof becomes a vertex in a graph linking identities to completed work, and peers only trade with identities whose graph reaches a summit of accumulated proofs. An attacker pays the compute cost for every fake, so ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand times the work of one honest agent.
